title: Local demographic history does not reduce to static island architecture in Antarctic penguins
central_claim: Dynamic within-island biological state can carry short-lived demographic history even when static breeding-island architecture does not yield a confirmed, scale-invariant response rule across Antarctic penguin populations.

part_I.concentration_claim: Palmer Adelie decline includes within-island concentration beyond proportional thinning plus prespecified count error.
part_I.state_claim: A late-season colony-wide state predicts later within-island redistribution under the fixed-specification lag analysis after shared island-transition growth, prior group size and persistent colony identity are controlled.

primary_bias_resistant_lag2.inference_status: fixed-specification validation after provenance repair; not fully outcome-blind preregistration

state_memory.role: mechanism diagnostic only; bridge is not causal mediation

independent_repro_validation.implication: Do not generalize the late-season colony-wide state as generic nest reproductive success.

part_I.arrival_gate: HUMPOP colony-level arrival endpoint stopped before coefficient fitting because the frozen information minimum was not met.

part_II.primary: 2 km A x H cross-species median gamma_AH = -0.318; 9999-permutation one-sided p = 0.0947; non-confirmatory
part_II.simple_buffering: A-only point estimates are negative in all three species but no Holm-adjusted rejection
part_II.radius: joint 2-to-5 km sign-switch-plus-contrast null p=0.081; radius sensitivity, not established scale dependence
part_II.power_boundary: MDE80 |gamma_AH|≈0.50 and MDE90≈0.54; moderate common effects near the observed magnitude remain unresolved

cross_scale_interpretation: The local result is not 'state beats place': Palmer terrain, snow and geomorphology remain biologically relevant.
The local result is that realized breeding-landscape value contains a dynamic historical component not captured by static colony identity or abundance alone.
The macro result is that static breeding-space amount and habitat-option heterogeneity do not compress that local complexity into a confirmed transferable Antarctic-wide rule.
The REPRO failure narrows the Palmer state to a late-season colony-wide biological state rather than generic reproductive success.

ross_status.role: prospective independent individual-level mechanism test, not current manuscript evidence
ross_status.manuscript_rule: Do not cite Ross coefficients, sample sizes, directions or results because none have been opened.

prohibited_language: Palmer lag analysis was fully preregistered or outcome-blind
biological scale dependence from the 1/2/5 km reversal
species-wide latent forcing is a specific identified climate driver
manuscript_priorities: Make late-season state and independent REPRO non-replication central to Part I.
Retain concentration as the spatial-demographic entry point rather than the final Palmer mechanism claim.
Keep Part II inferentially independent and non-confirmatory.
Frame the synthesis as dynamic local history versus limited transferability of static descriptors, not a state-versus-place dichotomy.
Keep provenance-repair and post-hoc diagnostic labels explicit.
Keep Ross Island outside the evidentiary Results until the exact-header gate is unlocked and outcomes are run.
